text: The question at the centre of the story cannot, in the nature of things, be answered; and Genesis 22 has in the end less to do with sacrifice than with reading. Whoever reads it closely learns that the most important things are those the narrative declines to say. Abraham is silent; Isaac asks his question; Sarah is nowhere present; the narrator gives no reason. Each of these is a gap in the text, and each lays its demand upon the reader of Abraham and Isaac.
